newsitem.title: GHANA: Thirty new companies join Ghana gold rush.
newsitem.headline: Thirty new companies join Ghana gold rush.

text.p: Thirty companies joined the search for gold in Ghana in the second half of 1996, taking the number of registered gold operators in the country to 217, Ghana Minerals Commission figures showed.
The number of foreign controlled exploration companies went up by 13 in the same period and now stands at 74. Ghanaian-owned prospecting companies increased by 17 to a total of 123.
The number of companies granted mining leases rose to 20 with two new entrants, Midras Co Ltd and Sian Goldfields Ltd.
Midras, fully owned by Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd, has a 7.3 sq km concession at Asikam in Ghana's Eastern Region.
Sian, an affiliate of Ghanaian timber group Primewood, was granted a mining lease for its 47 sq km concession at Esaase, also in the Eastern Region.
Ashanti, which accounts for more than two-thirds of Ghana's gold output, put its annualised rate of production last year at 1.1 million ounces, a rate it expects to maintain in 1997.
